problems.title: Rain Gauge Rectangle
problems.story: Rain Gauge Rectangle is an independent Quadrantcode practice scenario. A planning team has reduced its observations to an integer sequence and needs a precise largest contiguous rectangle result before the next decision can be made.
problems.statement: Implement the required function for Rain Gauge Rectangle. Interpret the supplied sequence exactly as described in the input contract, compute the largest contiguous rectangle, and return only the requested integer. The function must handle boundary cases and the largest stated input without modifying any external state.
problems.inputFormat: The array values contains nonnegative bar heights in left-to-right order.
problems.outputFormat: Return the greatest rectangular area supported by consecutive bars.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: The complete integer encoding described by this problem.

constraints: The result fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Example 1 follows the stated largest contiguous rectangle process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 10.
Example 2 follows the stated largest contiguous rectangle process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 4.

testCases.explanation: Applying the largest contiguous rectangle rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.
Applying the largest contiguous rectangle rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.

hints: A bar can extend until the first smaller bar on each side.
Use a monotonic increasing stack and finalize taller bars when a shorter bar arrives.

editorial.overview: Use a monotonic stack of starting positions and heights. Each pop finalizes the widest rectangle for that height.
editorial.bruteForceApproach: Choose every left boundary, extend right, maintain the minimum height, and evaluate each rectangle.
editorial.optimalApproach: Keep increasing heights with their earliest valid starts. A lower height closes all taller rectangles; a zero sentinel closes the rest.
editorial.correctnessProof: A popped height cannot extend through the current lower bar, and its stored start is the earliest position it can reach. Thus the computed width is maximal for that height. Every height is eventually popped, so the best rectangle is considered.

c11.referenceSolution: long long solve(const long long*v,int n){long long best=0,*h=malloc(sizeof(long long)*(n+1));int*s=malloc(sizeof(int)*(n+1)),top=0;for(int i=0;i<=n;i++){long long x=i<n?v[i]:0;int start=i;while(top&&h[top-1]>x){top--;if(h[top]*(i-s[top])>best)best=h[top]*(i-s[top]);start=s[top];}if(!top||h[top-1]<x){h[top]=x;s[top++]=start;}}free(h);free(s);return best;}

cpp17.referenceSolution: long long solve(const vector<long long>&v){vector<pair<int,long long>>st;long long b=0;for(int i=0;i<=(int)v.size();i++){long long h=i<(int)v.size()?v[i]:0;int s=i;while(!st.empty()&&st.back().second>h){auto p=st.back();st.pop_back();b=max(b,p.second*(i-p.first));s=p.first;}if(st.empty()||st.back().second<h)st.push_back({s,h});}return b;}

java.referenceSolution: static long solve(long[]v){int n=v.length,top=0;long[]h=new long[n+1];int[]s=new int[n+1];long best=0;for(int i=0;i<=n;i++){long x=i<n?v[i]:0;int start=i;while(top>0&&h[top-1]>x){top--;best=Math.max(best,h[top]*(i-s[top]));start=s[top];}if(top==0||h[top-1]<x){h[top]=x;s[top++]=start;}}return best;}

javascript.referenceSolution: function solve(v){const st=[];let b=0;for(let i=0;i<=v.length;i++){const h=i<v.length?v[i]:0;let s=i;while(st.length&&st[st.length - 1][1]>h){const p=st.pop();b=Math.max(b,p[1]*(i-p[0]));s=p[0];}if(!st.length||st[st.length - 1][1]<h)st.push([s,h]);}return b;}

The function must handle boundary cases and the largest stated input without modifying any external state.
problems.inputFormat: values[0] is k (one means the tail). values[1..] lists linked-list node values from head to tail.
problems.outputFormat: Return the value of the kth node from the end, or -1 when k is outside the chain.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: The complete integer encoding described by this problem.

constraints: Node values fit in signed 32-bit integers.

examples.explanation: Example 1 follows the stated reverse-rank chain lookup process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 30.
Example 2 follows the stated reverse-rank chain lookup process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 8.

testCases.explanation: Applying the reverse-rank chain lookup rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.
Applying the reverse-rank chain lookup rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.

hints: Move a lead pointer k nodes before moving a second pointer.
When the lead pointer reaches the end, the second pointer has the requested reverse rank.

editorial.overview: Interpret the payload after k as a singly linked chain and keep a fixed gap between two positions.
editorial.bruteForceApproach: Count all nodes, convert the reverse rank to a forward index, then traverse again.
editorial.optimalApproach: Advance a lead position k steps. If possible, advance lead and follower together until lead leaves the chain.
editorial.correctnessProof: The lead stays exactly k nodes ahead of the follower. When lead is one position beyond the tail, exactly k nodes including the follower remain from follower to tail, so follower is kth from the end.

c11.referenceSolution: long long solve(const long long*v,int n){if(n<2||v[0]<1||v[0]>n-1)return -1;return v[n-(int)v[0]];}

cpp17.referenceSolution: long long solve(const vector<long long>&v){return v.size()>1&&v[0]>=1&&v[0]<(long long)v.size()?v[v.size()-v[0]]:-1;}

python3.referenceSolution:
def solve(v: list[int]) -> int:
    return v[-v[0]] if len(v)>1 and 1<=v[0]<len(v) else -1

problems.title: Orchard Canopy Depth
problems.story: Orchard Canopy Depth is an independent Quadrantcode practice scenario. A planning team has reduced its observations to an integer sequence and needs a precise binary-tree depth result before the next decision can be made.
problems.statement: Implement the required function for Orchard Canopy Depth. Interpret the supplied sequence exactly as described in the input contract, compute the binary-tree depth, and return only the requested integer. The function must handle boundary cases and the largest stated input without modifying any external state.
problems.inputFormat: values is a level-order binary-tree array using -1 for a missing node. Children of index i are 2i+1 and 2i+2.
problems.outputFormat: Return the number of nodes on the longest root-to-present-node path; an empty or missing root has depth 0.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: The complete integer encoding described by this problem.

constraints: -1 marks absence and is not a node value
Every present non-root node has a present ancestor chain.

examples.explanation: Example 1 follows the stated binary-tree depth process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 3.
Example 2 follows the stated binary-tree depth process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 1.

testCases.explanation: Applying the binary-tree depth rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.
Applying the binary-tree depth rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.

hints: A level-order index determines its tree level.
Scan present nodes and retain the largest level, or traverse breadth first.

editorial.overview: Visit each present level-order entry and determine its one-based depth from its heap index.
editorial.bruteForceApproach: For each present node, repeatedly move to its parent and count steps to the root.
editorial.optimalApproach: Scan indices once while tracking the next power-of-two level boundary, updating the maximum for present nodes.
editorial.correctnessProof: Heap indices [2^(d-1)-1, 2^d-2] are exactly depth d. Every present node is inspected and assigned its exact depth, so the maximum assigned depth equals the longest root-to-node path.

c11.referenceSolution: long long solve(const long long*v,int n){if(!n||v[0]==-1)return 0;int d=1,next=1,b=0;for(int i=0;i<n;i++){if(i==next){d++;next=next*2+1;}if(v[i]!=-1&&d>b)b=d;}return b;}

cpp17.referenceSolution: long long solve(const vector<long long>&v){if(v.empty()||v[0]==-1)return 0;int d=1,next=1,b=0;for(int i=0;i<(int)v.size();i++){if(i==next){d++;next=next*2+1;}if(v[i]!=-1)b=max(b,d);}return b;}
